observations: Photo 0 shows a metal automotive alternator/charging component with cooling fins and a pulley area; no clear brand/model markings visible.
Photo 1 shows the same unit from another angle with a circular front face and mounting ears/holes; again no readable brand/model.
Photo 2 shows the rear side with a threaded shaft/stud and finned housing; no readable part number.

claims.evidence: No shipping/origin documents or labels visible in the photos.
Photos only; no test video, bench test report, or voltage/current readings.
No audio/video of running condition; photos cannot confirm internal noise.
No mileage/odometer data or part history shown; alternators don’t carry mileage in photos.
No seals/inspection marks or proof of non-disassembly visible.

claims.claim: Also deals on all kinds of cars spare parts.
claims.evidence: General business statement; not tied to this specific item.

risks.risk: Wrong part fitment (alternators vary by engine/model, pulley type, and electrical connector). Photos don’t show a readable part number.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label/part number (or stamping) plus the vehicle details the seller used (make/model/year/engine) and the connector/pulley type.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic alternator with unknown fitment risk (assume may not match).

risks.risk: Not actually working / weak output (alternators can look fine but fail under load).
risks.proof: Video of the alternator being tested (bench test or installed test) showing output voltage under load (e.g., idle and with headlights/blower).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working (assume needs testing/possible replacement).

risks.risk: Internal bearing/rotor issues causing noise or early failure (seller says 'no knock' but no running proof).
risks.proof: Short audio/video while running (or a bench spin test) showing no abnormal noise and stable output.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially noisy/defective until proven.

risks.risk: Missing accessories or incorrect pulley (some units come with different pulley sizes or may be missing brackets/parts).
risks.proof: Photo of everything included: pulley, mounting brackets, regulator/connector area, and any included hardware; plus close-ups of pulley markings/size.

proof_requests: Send a close-up photo of any readable part number/label/stamping on the alternator (front, side, and rear).
Tell the exact vehicle fitment: make/model/year/engine (and whether it’s for petrol/diesel).
Provide a test proof: bench test or installed test video with voltage readings (idle and with load).
Show the pulley type/size and confirm what is included (pulley, brackets, regulator/connector).
response.reason: The photos show an alternator-like car charging part, but there’s no readable part number or test evidence. Seller claims about working condition and noise cannot be verified remotely, so proof is needed before a reliable price.
